operators.notes: Sequential scan of o_custkey.bin (60MB). Build a bitset[0..1500000] marking all custkeys that have at least one order. Parallel morsel scan, each thread ORs bits into shared bitset using atomic 64-bit ops.

First pass over customer. Extract 2-char phone prefix, check membership in 7-element set, filter c_acctbal > 0. Compute thread-local SUM and COUNT, then reduce to global AVG. Phone prefix check: parse first 2 bytes of c_phone varlen, compare against compile-time constant set.

Second pass over customer. Fused filter → anti-join check → aggregate pipeline. Apply predicates in selectivity order: (1) phone prefix IN set (eliminates ~72%), (2) c_acctbal > avg (eliminates ~50% of remainder), (3) bitset anti-join (eliminates ~67% of remainder — most customers have orders). Thread-local aggregation into 7-bucket array indexed by cntrycode, then reduce across threads.
Trivial: merge per-thread 7-bucket arrays (SUM counts, SUM totacctbals), then sort 7 rows by cntrycode. Single-threaded, O(1).

data_structures.orders_custkey_bitset: bitset(1500001) — 187KB, fits in L3 cache. Indexed by c_custkey value. Bit set = customer has ≥1 order.
data_structures.phone_prefix_set: compile_time_constant_array — 7 two-char codes stored as uint16_t for branchless comparison
data_structures.subquery_accumulators: thread_local_pair(sum: double, count: int64) — one per thread, reduced after step 2
data_structures.aggregation_buckets: direct_array(7) per thread — indexed by cntrycode mapped to 0..6. Each bucket: {count: int64, sum_acctbal: double}

parallelism.step1_morsels: 65536 rows per morsel over o_custkey scan
parallelism.step2_morsels: 65536 rows per morsel over customer scan
parallelism.step3_morsels: 65536 rows per morsel over customer scan (second pass)
parallelism.notes: Steps 1 and 2 are independent and can execute concurrently (different tables). Step 3 depends on both. Step 4 is single-threaded finalization of 7 rows.

concurrent_steps.notes: Steps 1 (orders bitset build) and 2 (customer AVG subquery) read different tables and can run in parallel. Allocate ~32 threads each. Step 3 waits for both, then uses all 64 threads.
